title: Reading export
description: One run of the code-semantics reading: what subject matter a repository is concerned with, and the evidence for it. `summary` carries the result. `signals`, `themes` and `taxonomies` carry one piece of evidence per entry. `setAside` counts what the reading measured and these lists omit.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: The version of this document's shape. It rises when a field is added, renamed or removed. Consuming code branches on it.

summary.title: Result
summary.description: The whole result. Every figure here also appears in a list below.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: The name of the directory the reading was pointed at.

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: The commit the working tree stood on, supplied by the caller. The reading opens no .git, so this is empty where the caller supplied nothing.

answers.title: What the repository is about
answers.description: Every source that cleared the bar of the first rung to qualify, ranked. A published vocabulary's terms of more than one word answer first, because a repository outside a field does not write `cap floor` or `msg seq num` by accident and the publisher states what the run means; then the same vocabularies' one-word terms, which carry no permutation bar and are admitted only where the repository writes another concept from the same branch; then every subject scheme level standing apart from chance, where nothing is matched at all and the answer is a distance. The rungs still back off — a reading answered by a subject scheme is one whose vocabularies said nothing — but within the rung that answers, nothing is dropped for coming second. A reading with no qualifying evidence holds one entry saying so. Every rung's own figures stay in `taxonomies` and `summary.placedIn` beneath it.

items.title: One source's statement of what the repository is about
items.description: What one qualifying source says the repository is, and what that rests on. Every source that cleared the same rung's bar is listed, ranked by how far it cleared it, because naming only the best of them hides the rest: on a card-payment library five vocabularies clear the phrase bar and only one of them places its concept under `Cards`.

sourceType.description: What kind of thing answered: `taxonomy` for a vocabulary of terms matched identifier to identifier, `subject scheme` for a scheme of published prose diverged against, or `nothing`.

source.description: The publisher, under the name it states. Empty where nothing answered.

statedPath.title: Where the publisher places what answered
statedPath.description: Every level the publisher states above what answered, broadest first, with the levels naming the publisher's own field stepped over — the levels an outright majority of the vocabulary sits beneath, which name only the vocabulary that matched. Empty where the publisher states nothing above it, which FpML does for 616 of its 1,405 types. It is the whole path and not its two ends: FIX places 5,434 of its 7,170 rows one level down, so the two ends were the same label on those, and FIBO states `Aspect → Value → QuantitativeValue → PresentValue`, where the two ends dropped `Value`. For a subject scheme it is the archive the answering category sits in, and empty where the archive is itself the answer.

result.description: What that publisher says this repository is. For a taxonomy it is the publisher's own definition of the concept the repository wrote most, named before it — the node carries the meaning, and reporting only its name would have matched a name. A concept the publisher defines nothing for is passed over for the next one written, which is Katz backoff at the answer; where the vocabulary defines none of what was matched, what the vocabulary covers is the most the publishers say. Answering at the branch or at the vocabulary was tried and is the `blocking` failure of hierarchical classification — stopping at an internal node when the evidence supports descending. For a subject scheme it is the subject itself.

qualifiedBy.description: How it cleared its own bar, in the unit that bar is set in.

timesItsBar.title: Times its own chance bar
timesItsBar.description: How many times the count a deal of its own words reaches this vocabulary's phrase count came to. Present only where `sourceType` is `taxonomy`: a subject scheme faces no permutation bar, and a source that cannot speak in a unit leaves the field out rather than writing a zero into it.

bitsPastChance.title: Bits nearer than chance reached
bitsPastChance.description: How much nearer the repository stood to this subject than the nearest subject of a scheme of chance stood. Present only where `sourceType` is `subject scheme`: a vocabulary states no distance, and the two strengths are different quantities that are never stated in one another's unit.

about.title: Subjects that distinguish some part of the repository
about.description: The topics accounting for the departure of at least one scope from the whole repository. A topic written at the same density everywhere contributes almost nothing to a divergence and appears here for no scope.

aboutStatedBy.title: What named the subjects
aboutStatedBy.description: The resources whose labels the `about` topics are. They are not a taxonomy's concepts: they are the labels dictionaries put on the senses of the words the repository declares, and a consumer reading `linguistics` beside a concept should be able to tell which kind of answer it has.

placedIn.title: Where every bundled scheme places it
placedIn.description: One entry per published subject scheme, each drawn against its own null. No scheme is picked: a scheme whose nearest subject is no nearer than chance stands here saying so, which is a result rather than an omission.

leadingWords.title: Words with the highest scores
leadingWords.description: The words scoring highest against every reference, highest first, each with the score that put it there. `signals` carries the same words with the line each was first written on.

word.description: The word as the identifier splitter produced it.

divergenceBits.description: Its term of the Jensen-Shannon divergence against the reference scoring it lowest, bounded at 1 bit.

occurrences.description: How many times the repository writes it.

leadingConcepts.title: Published concepts written most
leadingConcepts.description: The concepts of a published vocabulary the repository writes most of, weighted by specificity, taken across every vocabulary matched rather than the first. `taxonomies` carries each one with the concept its publisher places it under.

publishedBy.description: The vocabulary publishing this concept, which decides what it means and how far to trust it.

distinctiveScopes.title: Scopes exceeding chance resampling
distinctiveScopes.description: The scopes whose divergence from the whole repository exceeds all 999 resamples of a scope of their own size.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: One directory the build compiles as a unit, such as `lexicon/src/main/java`, or the repository's documentation.

divergenceBits.title: Divergence in bits
divergenceBits.description: The Jensen-Shannon divergence between this scope's distribution over subjects and the whole repository's. Base-2 logarithms bound it at 1 bit.

writesMoreOf.title: Topics accounting for the divergence
writesMoreOf.description: The topics this scope writes at a higher density than the repository does. Each also appears in `summary.about`.

shareOfWordsWithACitation.title: Share of word occurrences a resource covers
shareOfWordsWithACitation.description: The share of word occurrences at least one bundled resource has an entry for. Every other figure rests on this denominator: a word no resource covers is counted here and contributes evidence nowhere.

shareOfMassOnNoSubject.title: Share of evidence resolving to no subject
shareOfMassOnNoSubject.description: The share of observed evidence that resolves to no subject. A word can have a dictionary entry and still say nothing about subject matter, so this figure runs high alongside a high `shareOfWordsWithACitation`.

counts.title: Length of each list
counts.description: How many entries each list below holds.

signals.title: Signals
signals.description: Every word and published phrase the repository writes at a higher density than each reference it is scored against. Words English supplies inside a name — `by`, `from`, `beside` — are scored, ranked and omitted here, because writing one is not a choice about subject matter; the vocabulary report prints them under their own heading. `setAside.wordsTheLanguageSupplies` counts them; `setAside.wordsBelowEveryThreshold` counts the words that scored below a threshold.

readFrom.title: Source read
readFrom.description: Which source supplied the signal. CLONE is the working tree.

word.title: Word
word.description: The word as the identifier splitter produced it. A run of words a topical resource publishes as one entry keeps its spaces: `part of speech` is one word here.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: How many times the repository writes it.

occurrencesInNames.title: Occurrences in declared names
occurrencesInNames.description: How many of those occurrences are a declared name rather than prose. `citationSource` contributes to this count; the javadoc above it does not.

divergenceBits.title: Score in bits
divergenceBits.description: This word's term of the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the repository's word distribution and the reference's. Base-2 logarithms bound it at 1 bit. A word the repository writes at the reference's own density scores 0.

marginBits.title: Score at the reference's own error
marginBits.description: The same term computed with the reference's share moved one standard error toward the repository's — the score with the reference's own sampling error held against the word. The verdict rests on it: every signal's margin exceeds every reference's chance threshold, and a word whose score clears the thresholds while its margin does not is counted in `setAside.wordsWithinTheReferencesError` instead of listed here.

closestReference.title: Reference giving the lowest score
closestReference.description: The reference scoring this word lowest, which is the score reported. `get` scores high against ordinary English and low against the Java platform's own API, so the platform is its closest reference.

thresholds.title: Chance thresholds
thresholds.description: The threshold each reference's own permutation null sets for this repository, in bits, keyed by the reference's name. A signal's marginBits exceeds every one of them, and marginBits divided by a threshold states how far outside chance the word stands.

themes.title: Themes
themes.description: Each topic the reading reports, in the scope whose divergence it accounts for. One topic accounting for two scopes' divergences appears twice, once per scope.

topic.title: Topic
topic.description: The label the topic resource publishes, in that resource's own spelling.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: The scope whose divergence from the repository this topic accounts for.

shareOfRepository.title: Share of observed evidence
shareOfRepository.description: This topic's share of all evidence the reading observed, resolved to a subject or not. The denominator includes what resolved to nothing, so the figure states how much of what the repository wrote carries the topic.

divergenceBits.title: Term of the divergence in bits
divergenceBits.description: How much of the scope's total divergence this topic accounts for. The terms across all topics sum to the scope's `divergenceBits`.

carriedBy.title: Words producing the score
carriedBy.description: The words contributing most of this topic's score with the evidence for each, largest contribution first. One word here means one word produced the topic.

taxonomies.title: Taxonomy evaluations
taxonomies.description: One entry per published vocabulary the repository's declared names were matched against. No entry states a subject placement: the placements this reading computes are the vocabulary reading's, over the dictionary topics of the words a repository declares, and they are stated under `summary.placedIn`, one per scheme. Only a vocabulary whose count exceeds its bar appears here; `setAside.vocabulariesBelowTheirChanceBar` carries a row for each of the rest, with the bar it failed.

vocabulary.title: Vocabulary matched against
vocabulary.description: The published vocabulary supplying the concepts, under the name its publisher states. OLiA is the Ontologies of Linguistic Annotation.

concepts.title: Concepts the repository writes
concepts.description: Every concept of that vocabulary the repository writes, largest specificity times occurrences first. A term of one word appears only where the repository also writes another concept from the same branch; a term of more than one word appears unconditionally, because ordinary English sentences contain few of them.

concept.title: Concept
concept.description: The label the publisher states, such as OLiA's `AdjectivePhrase`.

term.description: The run of words the repository wrote to reach the concept. It is not the concept's label: a two-word term reaches a concept CSO labels `capital`, so a reading carrying only the label cannot say which phrase was written.

normalisation.title: Level the two sides were compared at
normalisation.description: What both sides were normalised to before they were compared, which is one of the levels `matchesByNormalisation` counts. `bar.phrases` counts the rows at `words` only, so a row at `lemmas`, `expansions` or `senses` is a match the bar did not test: `payment date` reaches FpML's `PaymentDates` at `lemmas`.

definition.description: What the publisher says the concept means, empty where it states nothing. It is the whole reason a taxonomy is matched rather than a word list: the node carries the meaning, and a reading that reaches a node and drops its definition has matched a name.

description.title: Nearest prose the publisher states
description.description: The prose the publisher states at or above the concept, taken from the nearest level that states any, and empty where no level does. It equals `definition` wherever the publisher describes the concept itself. CSO states no prose for `public keys` and places it under `public key cryptography`, which the Wikipedia article CSO's own `owl:sameAs` names is summarised for, so the summary describes the match. A level an outright majority of the vocabulary sits beneath is stepped over, because naming it says only which vocabulary matched.

descriptionStatedFor.title: Concept the description is stated for
descriptionStatedFor.description: The concept `description` is stated for: this concept where the publisher describes it, the level the walk climbed to where it does not, and empty where nothing describes it at any level. A summary of `public key cryptography` is not a definition of `public keys`, so a report printing the one prints the other.

placedUnder.title: Concept the publisher places it under
placedUnder.description: The publisher's own parent for this concept, empty at a root of the taxonomy. OLiA places `Verb` under `WordClass`.

statedPath.description: Every level the publisher states above this concept, broadest first, with the levels naming the publisher's own field stepped over. `placedUnder` is the raw `broader` cell and this is the whole walk: a concept FIX places directly under `Common` states `placedUnder` as `Common` and an empty path, because `Common` holds 68% of FIX and names only the vocabulary that matched.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: How many times the repository writes the term inside a declared name.

specificity.title: Specificity
specificity.description: How far the term narrows the subject matter, computed as log(rank)/log(size) against a published frequency list, which bounds it in [0, 1] by its own length. `name` scores near 0; `interest rate swap` scores near 1.

wordsInTerm.title: Words in the published term
wordsInTerm.description: How many words the published term is written in. A term of one word is what a repository outside the vocabulary's domain matches by accident, so those terms carry the branch condition described under `concepts`.

shareOfEachName.title: Share of each name the term accounted for
shareOfEachName.description: The mean share of what each declared name narrows that this term accounted for. `Source` inside `EvidenceSource` accounts for two thirds of what that name narrows; a term written as a whole name accounts for all of it. It weights nothing: weighting the term's mass by it was measured on the evaluation set and lowered the ranking, so the figure is reported and not applied.

branches.title: What each branch is worth against this repository
branches.description: One entry per branch the repository wrote a concept in, most-carried first. `agreesWithTheRepository` is the mass this repository's reading and the prose the publisher states beneath that branch put in the same dictionary topics, bounded in [0, 1] by that statistic's own definition. It is reported and applied to nothing: `concepts` above is ordered by unconditioned mass, and `kept` states what conditioning on this weight would leave. Empty where the publisher states no prose — CSO describes none of its 14,636 rows, so its branches cannot be weighed, which is not the same as weighing zero.

branch.description: The concept the publisher places these under.

agreesWithTheRepository.description: How much of what the branch is about the repository is also about.

mass.description: What the repository wrote in this branch: occurrences weighed by how much each term narrows, unconditioned.

kept.description: That mass at this branch's weight. The difference from `mass` is what conditioning would set apart, and nothing is removed from the evidence.

terms.description: The terms matched in this branch, most-carried first.

matchesByNormalisation.title: Matches per normalisation level
matchesByNormalisation.description: How many matches each level produced. The levels are reported separately and never summed: a term found in the words exactly as written and a term found in what a dictionary says those words mean carry different weight as evidence.

words.description: Both sides compared as the words each writes, exactly as written. `adjectivePhrase` matches OLiA's `AdjectivePhrase`.

lemmas.description: Both sides reduced to each word's dictionary form, from [WordNet](https://wordnet.princeton.edu/). `phrases` matches `Phrase`.

expansions.description: Both sides with a shortened word written out as the expansion [Wiktionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/) cites for it, then reduced to dictionary forms. `extract info` matches `extracting information`. A token several sources expand differently — `msg` as message, Madison Square Garden and monosodium glutamate — is not expanded at all, because nothing in the citations ranks them.

senses.description: Both sides taken as the meaning of each word, normalised to a [WordNet](https://wordnet.princeton.edu/) sense, and only where WordNet holds the whole phrase as one entry. Reading a run word by word was tried and made two words sharing a commonest sense into one word, matching `set window` to `PutWindow` and `packet header` to `PackageHeader`. Reported, and contributing to no other figure in this document.

setAside.title: What the lists omit
setAside.description: What the reading measured and the three lists above omit: a count for each rule that removed something, and a row for each vocabulary the reading judged and refused. The rows behind the counts are in the generated reports.

wordOccurrencesNoResourceCovers.description: Word occurrences no bundled resource has an entry for. They remain in the denominator of `summary.shareOfWordsWithACitation`.

wordsBelowEveryThreshold.description: Words the reading scored that fall below the threshold at least one reference's own permutation null produced. This and `wordsTheLanguageSupplies` are the two rules that remove a word, and adding both to `summary.counts.signals` gives every word the ranking scored. The words themselves, with the references that refused each and by how much, are in `evidence.json`.

wordsWithinTheReferencesError.description: Words whose scores clear every reference's threshold while the margin — the same score with the reference's own sampling error held against the word — does not. A reference's share is an estimate from a drawn sample, and a verdict that holds only at the estimate's exact value has not been shown to stand above chance.

wordsTheLanguageSupplies.description: Words that cleared every reference's threshold and are omitted anyway, because two published resources place them inside the language rather than in the dictionary — `by`, `from`, `beside`. English put the word inside a name, so writing it was not a choice about subject matter. It is below no threshold, which is why it is counted apart.

scopesWithinChance.description: Scopes whose divergence from the repository at least one of 999 chance resamples equalled or exceeded. Their figures appear in no list here.

matchesDiscardedByBranchRule.description: Terms of one word the repository writes without writing any other concept from the same branch of the taxonomy. The branch rule discards them.

vocabulariesBelowTheirChanceBar.description: One row per vocabulary matched against this repository and not published, because it wrote no more of their phrases than a deal of their own words reaches. Each carries the bar it failed, so the refusal can be argued with from this file: CSO states 14,259 terms and a permutation of its own word list reaches many accidental matches, so CSO clears a higher bar than OLiA on the same repository and is refused where OLiA is published. Their concepts are left out with them. Every vocabulary the reading judged is named either here or in `taxonomies`, and none in both.

vocabulary.description: The publisher's name for it, as `taxonomies[].vocabulary` states it.

termsWorkingJavaAlsoWrites.description: Terms of the matched vocabularies that the reference corpus of working Java has been shown to write, summed over every vocabulary. They are removed from the index before either side of `taxonomies[].bar` is counted, so a vocabulary is judged on the terms that are its own: FpML states MimeType and TimeZone beside CapFloor, and only a corpus says which is FpML's subject. It counts the vocabularies' terms and not this repository's matches, because counting matches needs the reading run twice.

filesTheParserCouldNotRead.description: Files the parse rejected. The reading counts them and continues, so a narrowed corpus stays a reported figure.

site.title: File and line
site.description: Where to read the evidence behind a figure.

file.description: The path relative to the root of the repository that was read.

line.description: The line within that file, counting from 1.

placement.title: Subject placement
placement.description: Where the reading places the repository in one published subject scheme, at both levels the scheme states. Some subject is always nearest, so `standsApartFromChance` is what makes a placement a result, and `nearerThanChance` is every subject that result cannot be told apart from.

scheme.description: The published subject scheme both levels come from, such as the arXiv category taxonomy.

archive.title: Nearest top-level grouping
archive.description: The nearest of the scheme's own top-level groupings, compared against every description pooled under it. Enough prose for the divergence to be stable, and broad enough that Computer Science says little about a Java library.

category.title: Nearest single subject
category.description: The nearest single subject the scheme publishes, compared against the few dozen words the scheme states for it alone. The weaker measurement and the sharper answer: read this to learn what the repository is about.

subject.description: The subject's own label, as the scheme publishes it.

divergenceBits.description: The Jensen-Shannon divergence between the repository's distribution and that subject's, in bits.

nearestByChanceBits.description: The divergence to the nearest subject of a scheme built by shuffling the real subjects' descriptions.

carriedBy.title: Topics the placement rests on
carriedBy.description: The dictionary topics the repository's reading and this subject's own description both put mass in, most shared first. Two readings are near because of the mass they put in the same places, so this is what makes the row arguable with — and each names the shares and the words behind it, so the row can be checked without reading another section.

nearerThanChance.title: Every subject chance cannot separate from the nearest
nearerThanChance.description: Every subject standing nearer than `nearestByChanceBits`, nearest first, this level's own `subject` among them. Naming one subject out of these states a precision the instrument does not have. The bound is the chance figure itself and no margin is chosen here; a consumer refining a match against a deeper taxonomy should condition on all of them rather than on the leader.

subject.description: The subject's own label, as the scheme publishes it.

divergenceBits.description: The Jensen-Shannon divergence between the repository's distribution and that subject's, in bits.

carriedBy.description: The dictionary topics it and the repository both put mass in.

quotation.title: Quotation
quotation.description: The phrase a word was read in, and where it was written. The unit of the reading is the phrase and never the word, so the evidence shown is the phrase too.

phrase.description: The phrase the word was read in.

witness.title: Witness
witness.description: One word's testimony for a topic. Occurrences and mass disagree and both are stated: a word written five hundred times can carry almost no mass where the frequency list says it narrows nothing.

word.description: The word as the splitter produced it.

occurrences.description: How often the word was written.

mass.description: How much of the topic's mass this word carried.

sources.description: The resources naming this topic for this word, in their own published spelling. One resource here means one resource read the topic, which no other corroborated.

quotations.description: The phrases the word was read in, with where each was written.

carryingTopic.title: One topic a placement rests on
carryingTopic.description: A dictionary topic the repository's reading and the subject's own description both put mass in, with the two shares it met on and the words that put the repository's mass there. Stated in full rather than left to a join against `themes`, which reports only the scopes that depart from the whole: a label carries the same words wherever it appears, so they repeat across levels and a reader following one placement gets the whole answer in one place.

topic.title: Topic
topic.description: The dictionary label the two met on.

shareOfRepository.title: Share of the repository
shareOfRepository.description: The topic's share of everything the repository placed.

shareOfSubject.title: Share of the subject
shareOfSubject.description: The topic's share of the subject's own description, read by the same instrument.

carriedBy.title: Words that carried it
carriedBy.description: The words that put the repository's mass in this topic, most first. Fewer than a `themes` row holds: the placement is the answer and the whole tail is in `themes` and in the evidence beside it.

chanceBar.title: How the vocabulary's phrase count stands against chance
chanceBar.description: What a deal of this vocabulary's own words reaches on this repository, and how far its real count stands above that. The reference holds the repository still and deals the vocabulary: it keeps how many terms the publisher states, how long each is and its whole list of words, and destroys only which of its words it published beside which. A vocabulary whose word list is what reached the repository scores the same either way; one whose published orders reached it loses them. Dealing the repository instead would answer a different question, because declared names are compositional and a deal of them puts a vocabulary's words together in orders nobody wrote.

phrases.description: How many of the vocabulary's terms of more than one word the repository writes at the `words` level, counted once each however often it wrote them. The deals are taken at that level too, so both figures here are the words the two sides wrote and neither counts a match a dictionary reached. `concepts` lists matches at all four levels and states which on every row, so the rows at `words` are the ones this count tested. A term the reference corpus of working Java has been shown to write is removed from the vocabulary before this is counted, so what is counted is the publisher's own vocabulary.

chanceExpectedBest.description: The count the best of a field this size reaches by chance alone, read off the deals at the quantile the field sets. Every vocabulary is tested at once, so the bar is what the best of them would reach and not what one of them would.

median.description: The middle of the deals, so a reader can see both bars rather than one.

timesTheBar.description: `phrases` divided by `chanceExpectedBest`. It is not comparable between two readings whose vocabularies lost different numbers of terms to the corpus, because the bar moves with the count.

atLeastAsExtreme.description: How many of the deals reached the observed count or beat it.

chanceRate.description: How often chance alone produced a count this large: `(atLeastAsExtreme + 1) / (resamples + 1)`, bounded in [1/1000, 1] by the estimator's own definition. This is the one figure on the bar that compares two vocabularies of different sizes, because it is a probability rather than a count. `phrases` scales with how many terms the publisher states — BIAN states 319 and CSO 14,259 — and `timesTheBar` scales with the bar, so neither orders two vocabularies against each other.

field.description: How many vocabularies competed, which is what sets the quantile the bar is read at.
